issue.title: Bug: wait_until enhancement in test_acl_outer_vlan is redundant and causes test failure

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

PR #22978 replaced time.sleep(timeout) with wait_until(timeout, 2, 0, _check_acl_counter) in get_acl_counter(), introducing two bugs:

Bug 1: timeout=0 causes unconditional test failure
The first counter read calls get_acl_counter(..., timeout=0) to snapshot the counter value before sending traffic — no waiting is needed. The original time.sleep(0) returned immediately, which was correct. However, wait_until(0, 2, 0, _check_acl_counter) returns False with a zero timeout, triggering pytest.fail unconditionally.

Bug 2: wait_until checks the wrong condition, resulting in stale counter reads
The original time.sleep(timeout) inside get_acl_counter() waited a fixed duration for orchagent to flush updated counters to the aclshow output. The replacement _check_acl_counter only verifies that the ACL rule exists in aclshow -a output — it does not check whether the counter value has actually been updated. Since the rule is already present before any traffic is sent, wait_until succeeds immediately on the second call without waiting for the counter to refresh. This causes count_after to read the same stale value as count_before, leading to false test failures.

Root cause
The purpose of the timeout in get_acl_counter() is to allow time for orchagent to update the counters, not to poll for the aclshow -a command to succeed. The command is expected to work — if it doesn't, the test should fail. Replacing a wait-for-update sleep with a poll-for-command-output check misunderstands the intent.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run acl/test_acl_outer_vlan.py

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

The test should pass

resolution.title: Revert "[acl] Replace time.sleep with wait_until in test_acl_outer_vlan (#22978)"
resolution.description:
### Description of PR

Summary:
This reverts commit d11d9a5d6154b1e7705ebb6b0dbc1be620f578bf
which breaks get_acl_counter:
1. timeout=0 on the first poll makes wait_until fail immediately instead
of reading the counter without waiting.
2. The second poll returns instantly because wait_until only checks rule
existence, not counter freshness — reading stale values and causing
false failures.

The original time.sleep(timeout) works correctly — it gives orchagent
time to flush updated counters, which is the actual intent.

Fixes #25689
